disclaimer: EXPLORATORY AND POST-HOC. This analysis measures a property of the FROZEN V5 instrument's frontier-selection rule. It MUST NOT be used to re-score V5, to reinterpret any V5 verdict, to select a different level for any mechanism, or to promote any representation. V5's recorded sentinel CURRENT_SOLVER_OR_TASK_FAMILY_CANNOT_SUPPORT_GAME_R_MEASUREMENT and its artifact (sha256 0c5b3271c772bcaf304af65ae469d615572022d18ac81f3083b27a88b0097579) stand unchanged. No representation was ever scored under V5; only the control candidate V5E_L3_JSON_AST was measured. Zero model calls were made by this analysis.

1_implementation_verification.method: source read as TEXT; arena.experiments.fitness_v5 was never imported or executed

evidence.note: candidates are the sorted levels >= 1; the (distance, level) key with min() over an ascending list reproduces 'ties to the lower level'.

evidence.code: verdict = ('VOID_CEILING' if accuracy > high else 'VOID_FLOOR' if accuracy < low else 'FRONTIER_SELECTED')

evidence.note: in summarize(); the gap is a plain difference of the two accuracies

construction_evidence.note: the SAME `destroyed` CanonicalState object and the SAME default `options` tuple are passed to both siblings; only expected_index differs (0 vs 1).
identity and opposite-target are ASSERTED at construction, per family.

the prompt is a pure function of (genome, probe.question, probe.state, probe.options). Neither `variant` nor `expected_index` reaches the prompt, so the two destroyed siblings send byte-identical prompts.
both identifiers are placed at identical depth, so the question has no structural answer: content preserved, relation removed.

destroyed_control_is_a_structural_consta.arithmetic: A deterministic solver returns one answer to the shared prompt. That answer matches exactly one of the two opposite targets, so each twin pair contributes exactly 1 correct of 2. Over any number of families the destroyed accuracy is exactly 0.5000.
contingencies: Requires solver determinism (temperature 0, fixed seed). Held: all 24 twin pairs across the two measured cells (12 + 12) produced byte-identical prompt hashes AND byte-identical raw output, 24 correct of 48 rows.

Requires a valid parse on both twins. An unparsed row scores INCORRECT rather than voiding, so an invalid destroyed row pushes destroyed accuracy BELOW 0.5, never above. Held: valid_response_rate 1.000 everywhere in Phase 5.
Therefore destroyed <= 0.5 always, with equality under determinism + validity.

effective_qualifying_window.derivation: gap = positive - destroyed >= 0.20 with destroyed == 0.5000 <=> positive >= 0.70. The frontier ceiling caps positive at 0.85. Hence the qualifying window on positive accuracy is [0.70, 0.85], not the documented band [0.35, 0.85].
effective_qualifying_window.dead_gate: `negative_target_accuracy <= 0.60` is unconditionally satisfied because destroyed <= 0.5000 always. It carries zero information and cannot fire.

defect_provenance.finding: The incoherence was introduced by a single uncoordinated constant edit between V4 and V5, not by a deliberate design choice.
defect_provenance.implication: Under V3/V4 the gap threshold of 0.10 implied a window of [0.60, 0.85] and the 0.625 target sat INSIDE it (0.025 above the floor), so the selector was coherent. V5 raised the gap to 0.20 (justified in FITNESS_V5_SPEC.md section 5 by the gap's standard error of 0.142) and left the frontier target at 0.625. That single edit moved the window floor from 0.60 to 0.70 and stranded the selector's aim point 0.075 below the region it must land in.

1_implementation_verification.verdict: The premise is CONFIRMED as an arithmetic and design fact. The frozen selector targets 0.625, which the implementation's own gates make unqualifiable. A mechanism whose ladder happens to contain a level near 0.625 is voided with probability approaching 1, by construction.

2_frozen_phase5_gate_matrix.framing: POST-HOC re-analysis of already-collected rows. The ladder scan evaluated only the ORIGINAL and COUNTERFACTUAL (positive) arms at every level; the destroyed and swapped arms and the shortcut audit ran ONLY at the selected frontier (fitness_v5.py:1050 for the ladder scan; :1070-1075 for the single full-family evaluation at the selected level). Off-frontier destroyed accuracy is therefore IMPUTED at the structural constant 0.5000 and off-frontier position invariance and shortcut status are UNMEASURED. They cannot be recovered without new model calls, which were not made.
2_frozen_phase5_gate_matrix.central_question: Is there ANY level in the frozen ladder that satisfies every gate simultaneously?
2_frozen_phase5_gate_matrix.answer_detail: No level of any mechanism passes. Only ONE of the nine (mechanism x L1..L3) cells in the entire frozen ladder has a positive accuracy inside the effective window [0.70, 0.85]: precondition_conjunction L1 at 0.7083 - and the frozen selector already chose exactly that cell, where the binding failure was the answer-share gate (0.7917 > 0.75), not the gap. Every other cell is either above the 0.85 ceiling (formal_expression_depth L1 = 0.8750, transitive_dependency L1 = 0.9167) or below the 0.70 floor (0.5417, 0.5417, 0.5000, 0.5000, 0.6667, 0.5000). transitive_dependency is additionally dead at L0 (0.8750 < 0.90). Because the positive-accuracy gate alone excludes every non-selected level, the unmeasured off-frontier gates cannot change this answer.
2_frozen_phase5_gate_matrix.selector_cost_note: The selector's theoretical defect cost Phase 5 NOTHING. The only in-window cell that existed was the one the frozen selector picked.

3_simulated_operating_characteristics.framing: Explicit generative model, described in research/selector_analysis/selector_simulation.py. n = 24 positives per level (12 ORIGINAL + 12 COUNTERFACTUAL, balanced targets), independent-error binary forced choice, destroyed control fixed at the structural constant 0.5000, 20,000 replicates per profile (200,000 per null), 44 profiles sweeping (p at L1) x (decay rate). Q0, valid rate, truncation and the shortcut audit are assumed PASS and are not simulated; the shortcut audit is a probe-set property and is identical across selectors.

selectors.current_target_0.625: the frozen rule: argmin |acc - 0.625| over L1..L3
selectors.window_midpoint_0.775: same rule aimed at the midpoint of the effective window
selectors.highest_qualifying: deepest level that passes every gate; selects on the outcome
selectors.midpoint_0.80_gap0.25_calibrated: aims at 0.80 and raises the gap to 0.25 (i.e. accuracy >= 0.75) so that its coin-flipper false-positive rate matches the current selector's
selectors.oracle_knows_true_p: SENSITIVITY CEILING, not a proposal: picks the level whose TRUE accuracy is nearest the window midpoint, then applies the ordinary observed-data gates. Any real selector scoring above this is harvesting sampling noise.

sensitivity_loss_attributable_to_the_sel.interpretation: Against the achievable ceiling (a selector with perfect knowledge of the true profile) the frozen selector forfeits about 0.31 of absolute sensitivity - roughly 55% of the detectable cases. The naive fixes recover MORE than the ceiling, which is the tell that they are buying sensitivity from noise.

3_simulated_operating_characteristics.false_positive_reading: Strict nulls are well controlled by every selector: a constant answerer is rejected with probability 1 by the answer-share gate at every selector (share 1.000 > 0.75), and a coin-flipper that can still pass the explicit L0 arm is accepted 0.021 (current), 0.054 (window midpoint), 0.055 (highest-qualifying), 0.020 (calibrated). The decisive case is the NEAR-null: a genuine reader whose true accuracy is 0.65 flat - below the window floor - is accepted 0.074 (current), 0.533 (window midpoint), 0.587 (highest-qualifying), 0.360 (calibrated), 0.254 (oracle). Simply re-aiming the selector at 0.775 therefore buys 0.45 of sensitivity at the price of a 7x increase in near-threshold false positives. That is not an acceptable trade at n = 24.
3_simulated_operating_characteristics.where_the_selectors_agree: Per-profile agreement between the current and window-midpoint selectors is recorded in research/selector_analysis/selector_simulation.json under sweep[].selector_agreement_same_level / _same_verdict. They agree exactly when the ladder has no level between 0.625 and the window, which is the common case for steeply declining profiles and for profiles entirely below 0.625.
3_simulated_operating_characteristics.deeper_finding: The effective window [0.70, 0.85] is only 1.76 standard errors wide at n = 24. No selection rule can be simultaneously sensitive and specific against a target that narrow. Even a selector with perfect knowledge of the true profile qualifies a genuinely-in-band mechanism only 0.564 of the time and accepts a true-0.65 reader 0.254 of the time. The sample size, not the aim point, is the dominant limitation; the aim point is a real but second-order defect on top of it.

frozen_phase5_counterfactual._note: Off-frontier position invariance and the shortcut audit were never measured in Phase 5 (only positive arms ran off-frontier). Invariance is set to PASS and the shortcut audit is omitted, which can only FAVOUR the alternative selectors. EXPLORATORY: this does not re-score V5.

4_phase_6_implications.status: ANALYSIS ONLY. No Phase-6 artifact was read for modification or written.
4_phase_6_implications.primary_endpoint: paired exact McNemar on a degeneracy indicator (does the solver's answer equal solver A's modal answer) pooled over three FIXED cells - precondition_conjunction L2 and L3, transitive_dependency L3 - n = 72 (docs/PHASE6_PREREGISTRATION.md, PRIMARY ENDPOINT AND DECISION_RULE).
reasoning: The three cells are named in advance by (mechanism, level). They are not produced by select_frontier_level, so no property of that function enters the primary statistic.
The endpoint is a paired McNemar over discordant pairs on a per-probe indicator. It never reads positive_accuracy, positive_negative_gap, the frontier band or any qualification verdict.
The destroyed arms are not in the endpoint at all, so the 0.5000 constant is irrelevant to it.

The preregistration's own clause - 'Comparisons are made at FIXED levels, never at each solver's own selected frontier, since frontier selection on a statistic with SE ~ 0.10 could otherwise compare different tasks' - is precisely the immunisation this defect calls for, and it was written before any Phase-6 call.

could_a_no_band_conclusion_be_a_selector.answer: Not for the fixed-level comparison; PARTLY for any per-mechanism 'qualified' claim.
immune: the secondary per-mechanism ladder accuracy pooled over levels (all four levels enter; no selection)
the descriptive 12-cell accuracy grid, per-cell share and entropy
not_immune: any statement of the form 'mechanism M did not qualify under V5', which is a joint property of the ladder AND the selector
any comparison of QUALIFICATION VERDICTS between solvers, since two solvers with different ladders can be routed to different levels
could_a_no_band_conclusion_be_a_selector.empirical_bound_from_phase_5: For the Phase-5 solver the selector cost was exactly zero: re-running the frozen ladder under the window-midpoint, highest-qualifying and calibrated selectors yields 0 qualified mechanisms in every case, identical to the recorded result. A different solver's ladder could differ, so this bounds Phase 5, not Phase 6.
could_a_no_band_conclusion_be_a_selector.recommendation: Phase 6 should report per-mechanism qualification verdicts as DESCRIPTIVE ONLY (which its preregistration already does) and should additionally report the full L0..L3 positive-accuracy ladder for both solvers, so that a reader can see whether any level fell inside [0.70, 0.85] regardless of what the selector chose. That adds no calls: the ladder rows are already collected.

minimal_legitimate_future_correction.the_correction: In a FUTURE instrument version (V6+), make the frontier target a DERIVED quantity rather than a free constant: frontier_target = (positive_negative_gap_min + destroyed_expected + frontier_band_high) / 2, so that raising the gap threshold automatically moves the aim point and the two constants can never again drift apart. Additionally: delete negative_target_accuracy_max as a gate (it is unconditionally satisfied and carries no information), and state the effective window explicitly in the spec so the incoherence is visible on the page.
why_this_is_a_correction_and_not_protoco: It is derivable from the instrument's own definitions before seeing any outcome: the window [0.70, 0.85] follows from gap >= 0.20 and destroyed = 0.5000, both of which are frozen constants, and the 0.5000 is a theorem about the probe construction, not a measurement.
It changes WHERE the instrument measures, not WHETHER anything passes. The pass/fail thresholds are untouched.
Applied to the frozen Phase-5 data it changes NOTHING: 0 mechanisms qualify under every selector tested. A correction that cannot flip the existing result cannot be motivated by the existing result.
It removes a degree of freedom rather than adding one.
what_would_make_it_protocol_shopping: Lowering positive_negative_gap_min back toward 0.10, or raising frontier_band_high above 0.85, to make an already-observed cell pass. Those move a THRESHOLD in the direction of the observed data.

Adopting the 'highest level satisfying all gates' selector. It is selection on the qualification statistic itself; simulation shows it exceeds even the perfect-knowledge oracle's sensitivity (0.734 vs 0.564), which is proof it is converting noise into passes, and it raises near-threshold false positives from 0.074 to 0.587.
Re-running V5 or re-scoring the frozen artifact under any new selector. The V5 verdict is spent; a corrected selector may only be used on fresh probes.
Choosing the correction after inspecting which choice would let a favoured mechanism through.
what_must_be_preregistered_before_any_su: The derived frontier target and the explicit effective window, written out arithmetically in the spec.

That the destroyed control is a mathematical constant at 0.5000, with the consequence that the gap gate IS an absolute accuracy threshold, and a decision on whether to keep the destroyed arm at all - it currently consumes 24 of 72 calls per selected cell to measure a constant. Retaining it as an ASSERTION (that the solver is deterministic and the twins are identical) is defensible; retaining it as a negative control is not.
A power statement for the new window at the chosen n, including the simulated false-positive rate against a coin-flipper AND against a near-threshold reader below the window floor.

A ladder-granularity commitment. Phase 5's real limitation is that the ladders jump straight over the window (0.875 -> 0.542 and 0.917 -> 0.667); a finer ladder, or a per-mechanism difficulty knob, is needed before any selector can find an in-window level.

That the change is admissible under FITNESS_V5_SPEC.md section 9 only if it accompanies a change to a frozen variable class named in the prior failure analysis. A selector repair alone is explicitly 're-tuning thresholds' and does NOT license a new version on its own.

5_verdict.is_the_defect_real: YES - confirmed in the implementation, with traceable provenance
5_verdict.summary: The frozen V5 selector aims at 0.625 while its own gates make [0.70, 0.85] the only qualifying region. The destroyed-twin negative control is a mathematical constant at exactly 0.5000 (structurally, and verified 24/24 in the frozen rows), so the gap gate is an absolute threshold of positive_accuracy >= 0.70 and the destroyed <= 0.60 gate is dead. The incoherence entered when V5 raised the gap from V4's 0.10 to 0.20 without moving the target that V4's 0.10 had made coherent.
5_verdict.did_it_cost_phase_5_anything: NO. Exactly one of the nine candidate cells in the frozen ladder lies inside the effective window, and the frozen selector chose it. Under three alternative selectors the Phase-5 result is unchanged: 0 of 3 mechanisms qualify.
5_verdict.simulated_cost_in_general: Substantial but not cheaply recoverable. Against an achievable ceiling of 0.564, the frozen selector qualifies a genuinely-in-band mechanism 0.257 of the time. Re-aiming at the window midpoint raises that to 0.707 - above the ceiling - while raising acceptance of a true-0.65 reader from 0.074 to 0.533. The sensitivity is real; the naive fix does not deliver it honestly.
5_verdict.dominant_limitation: The effective window is 1.76 standard errors wide at n = 24, and both measured ladders step straight across it. Sample size and ladder granularity dominate the selector defect.
5_verdict.phase_6_impact: NONE on the primary endpoint; the fixed-level design is immune.
5_verdict.action_authorised_by_this_analysis: NONE. Reported for a future instrument version only.
